shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures ended lower on Friday on speculative selling and lingering hopes of de-escalation in the Black Sea grain export zone, traders said.

children: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures ended lower on Friday on speculative selling and lingering hopes of de-escalation in the Black Sea grain export zone, traders said.
CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) settled down 12-3/4 cents, or 1.75%, at $7.14-1/4 per bushel.

K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) ended down 10-3/4 cents, or 1.35%, at $7.83-3/4 a bushel and Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) fell 11-1/4 cents, or 1.5%, to finish at $7.41-1/4 a bushel.

Wheat traders said an AFP report, which cited a Turkish proposal sent to Russia and Ukraine for a truce on strikes against commercial shipping in the Black Sea, put investors' attention back on de-escalation prospects.
However, analysts were doubtful about any immediate breakthrough.

Western Australia is on track to produce 1 million metric tons more wheat than expected a month ago due to timely rains, the Grain Industry Association of Western Australia said in a monthly crop report.

After the close of the CBOT, weekly commitments data from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission showed that managed commodity funds erased their small net long position in CBOT wheat futures and flipped to a net short in the week to September 15.
